clearance.note: antennas: upright swivel dipoles on all four RP-SMA bulkheads (none chosen yet: typical 2.4 GHz swivel dipole, Ø10 x 108 (est; none chosen))

ball_path.note: every pan and tilt clear of the deck, the box and upright antennas by the margin; no firing within 60 deg of straight back (the operator's side)

fan.note: 9215-Y at full speed (12 V, 4000 rpm): 55.26 CFM free air, 2.87 mmH2O at zero flow (S06 p.2); straight-line curve between the two; blowing down into the fins.

operating_point.note: the J501's CFD of the bare box at 40 W in 25 C air

airflow.method: losses K x 0.5 rho v^2 (rho 1.2): K = 1 through the grille's gaps (the entry and the bars), K = 1 for the turn down into the fan on the whole flow across the duct over the fan's centre; the box's own resistance as k q^2 through the J501 CFD's operating point; the fan's straight-line curve from its J501 parameters (dp0, q_free); the new flow where the two meet
airflow.not_modelled: the open roof cells the shroud's floor covers (they vent through the 1 mm under it: intake_seal; bounded in the sensitivity), the deck over the exhaust, the fan's swirl
airflow.bench_proof: the thermometer, as the J501's own criterion: the box at 40 W (a 40 W nvpmodel under load) with the adapter on and the turret parked, a thermocouple in the collar 10 mm over the grille and one in the room 0.5 m away at the same height, logged for 30 min: the intake within 3 K of the room, and the module's temperatures from tegrastats no worse than for the same 30 min without the adapter (task N17)
airflow.note: hand estimate on the J501 0.9-g48r fan and its CFD's operating point (not converged: rerun this build when it settles); the mouth is as wide as the deck's front legs allow

intake_seal.note: the J501 roof is solid on top from the grille's openings out to its first open hex cell (the grille's rim, the skirt's top, a band of cells closed by a 1.2 mm skin: its cad/build.py); the foam ring lies in the middle of that band, so no exhaust cell opens inside it. The open cells under the shroud's floor vent through the 1 mm under it

shroud_fit.how: the BRepExtrema distance between the intake shroud and each leg (the deck cut round it, under the deck plate) and anything of the deck below its plate at each TM insert (none: the inserts are wholly in the 8 mm deck)

tipping.note: J501: 368 g printed (its slice report) + 1.0 kg Orin, carrier and cooler (est); a sideways push at the tilt axis that lifts the box off its narrow edge

overspeed.note: the fixed 12 V flywheel rail is the ceiling: at the X2216s' full no-load speed on it (10560 rpm) a ball leaves at about 19 m/s by this page's rough model (the physics' fastest ball at 100 % throttle on a fast motor and a high rail: 67.6 fps on Ø34 tyres, docs/turret-physics.md section 4), under the 70 fps cap; the barrel's two gates trip the safety line on any ball over 66 fps, and 24 V must never reach the ESCs

release.note: a ball that has already dropped still fires up to 103 ms after ARM is released; the phase-short brake (six FETs on the cartridge board, 5-14 ms after the line drops) stops the wheels to 5 % about 48 ms after release (docs/turret-physics.md section 5), where unbraked they would coast 1.1 s

checks.lid_screw: M3 x 40 ISO 4762, tip at z 62 (as the J501's own M3 x 16)

flywheel.note: the set speed for the nominal ball at the physics' set fps (sim/turret_launch3d.py); foam loss 30 % (assumed); the chronograph gates in the barrel measure the real speed

flight_level.note: a level shot from the bench (the box on a 0.3 m crate): [range m, time s, drop mm, speed m/s]; drag as a sphere, Cd 0.5

j501.cooler: Seeed reComputer mini J501 heatsink with fan (SKU 100099421): a G48R heat-pipe tower (Li Yang Peng) on a 2 mm copper spreader, 9215 fan 92 x 92 x 15 mm, 12 V
